stories.title: Community in 'shock' after several injured in crash
stories.summary: The local community is "shocked and devastated" following the crash in south Dublin yesterday in which six teenagers and a woman in her 40s were injured, a local councillor for Dún Laoghaire has said. A car mounted a footpath outside a row of shops on Oliver Plunkett Road in Monkstown Farm, Dún Laoghaire, at around 3pm. Three girls and three boys, aged between 13 and 15, were brought to CHI Temple Street and CHI Crumlin to be treated for a range of injuries, some described as critical. There have been reports the driver suffered a medical episode and lost control of the car, which then mounted the pavement. Another 15-year-old boy who witnessed the scene was taken to CHI Tallaght for medical attention. "Our thoughts are with the victims and their families, wishing them strength at this terrible time and hoping that they recover," she said, adding that some of the teenagers had suffered "life-changing injuries," Fine Gael Councillor Lorraine Hall said.

stories.title: Western railway platform extensions expected next year
stories.summary: Extensions of railway station platforms between Limerick and Athenry in Co Galway are expected to be completed by the end of the next year, as part of an effort to boost passenger capacity on the route. Iarnród Éireann is issuing tender documents for the construction works at five stations today. This will allow for six carriage trains to stop at Sixmilebridge, Ennis, Gort, Ardrahan and Craughwell. Platforms will be extended by 55 metres at four of the stations, with a 12 metre enhancement planned for Ennis. Iarnród Éireann said track enabling works are already under way and that it hopes to award a contract to the successful applicant by the end of the year. Chief Executive Mary Considine said the initiative will increase capacity and broaden transport options for those living close to the Galway - Limerick rail line.

stories.title: Derry not resting with work to be done ahead of 2027
stories.summary: Derry City claimed a seventh Club Orange Men's FAI Cup since 1985 yesterday. That's two more than any other club in that time period. Questions will now centre around whether the Candystripes can drive on and finally reach their potential, and the league crown that supporters so desperately crave. And while celebrations are in full swing in the north-west, immediate concern at the Ryan McBride Brandywell Stadium will turn to the question of who will be managing the club at the start of the 2027 season. The last time the club were in the cup final, Ruaidhrí Higgins left the club after Drogheda United upset them. Tiernan Lynch replaced him, but his reign came to an end this summer. Mark Connolly, appointed two months earlier as the Head of Football at the club, was thrust into the manager's job on an interim basis. "I think this went all right," he said at yesterday's post-match press conference.

Fans thought Rodrigo’s song also bore a similarity to Williams’ 2012 single Candy, which went to number one in the UK. The speculation prompted Williams to defend Rodrigo, saying he thinks a lot of plagiarism accusations in the music industry are not justified. He wrote on Instagram: "There’s something about the music industry that’s been bothering me for a while. "People coming after people because they’ve spotted a similarity between two songs. stories.title: Winners of the 2026 Food & Wine Restaurant of the Year Awards
stories.summary: The 2026 Food&Wine Restaurant of the Year Awards took place last night, celebrating the best of Ireland's hospitality industry. From neighbourhood gems to destination dining, the awards honour outstanding food, service, creativity and consistency across the country. This year's panel of judges consisted of a wide range of journalists and industry experts, including Ali Dunworth, Aoife Carrigy, Bairbre Power, Cathal McBride, Gillian Nelis, Joanne Cronin, Marcus O'Laoire, and the late Corinna Hardgrave, an esteemed restaurant critic who passed away this past October. This year's ceremony saw Artie Clifford of Blas na hÉireann inducted into the Food&Wine Restaurant of the Year Hall of Fame for 2026. Later in the evening, the most notable award of the night, 'Restaurant of the Year', went to The Lady Helen at Mount Juliet. The Michelin-starred restaurant is one of Ireland's most unique dining experiences, serving modern cuisine in a 260-year-old country manor, under the guidance of Chef John Kelly. The venue also took home the title of 'Pastry Chef of the Year' thanks to Tom Phelan, who just wrapped nine years of service at the restaurant, as well as 'Best Restaurant — Leinster 2026' and 'Best Chef — Leinster 2026'.

stories.title: Sides to discuss 'improved' 10.5% public sector pay offer
stories.summary: Trade unions and Government representatives will continue engagement today with an independent group in a bid to find a pathway to talks on the ongoing pay dispute. Over the weekend the Government made what it described as a "substantially improved" pay offer. It is understood the revised pay offer would deliver pay increases of 10.5% in an agreement that would run until the early months of 2029. This would equate to an 11% uplift when the increases are compounded over the duration of the agreement. There would be a bigger package and increases for lower paid public servants, with some benefitting by up to 17.8%. According to sources, the offer would include a payment of €1,200 or 2%, whichever is higher, in 2026, bringing pay increases for this year to 4% for public sector workers.

stories.title: Kingspan retains full year profit guidance for 2026
stories.summary: Insulation and building company Kingspan has today retained its full year profit guidance for 2026, adding that its pipeline continues to develop very positively. In a trading update in the period up to the end of September, Kingspan said that sales in the nine‐month period to the end of September rose by 10% to €7.6 billion from the same time last year. Sales were up 16% in the third quarter mainly due to strong underlying sales growth of 12%, it added. Co-Cavan based Kingspan said that while its end-markets have their obvious challenges the global backlog is ahead year on year, adding that there is still some way to go in the current year with much of the seasonally important fourth quarter remaining. "We continue to expect to deliver a full year trading profit in the region of €1,150m for the current year +20% versus 2025. Assuming our end-markets remain relatively stable, the strong backlog and pipeline ought to support a trading profit in the region of €1,470m in 202," it added. Kingspan said sales at its Insulated Building Envelopes sales rose by 4% in the first nine months and by 8% in the third quarter.

stories.title: Maya Jama quits Love Island after three years
stories.summary: Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as host of Love Island after three years, saying it is time to "throw myself into something new". The 32-year-old presenter, who recently appeared on The Celebrity Traitors, has fronted the ITV dating show since 2023, when she replaced Irish presenter Laura Whitmore. She has also hosted the spin-off series Love Island Games and Love Island: All Stars. Announcing her departure on Instagram, Jama said: "What an incredible era and what an unforgettable time I've had, it’s been far too much fun to put into words or a video, but as all good things must come to an end, it’s my time to step down as the host of my beloved Love Island." She thanked the show’s fans for their support and paid tribute to the production team. "I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the nine incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way. I’ve loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show. I’ll forever be grateful for the experience," she said.

stories.title: Could viral hair hacks be damaging your hair?
stories.summary: The likes of TikTok and Instagram have tried to convince us that growing thicker, longer and healthier hair is simply a matter of finding the right ingredient. Rosemary oil supposedly stimulates your follicles, scalp massagers allegedly encourage growth, and collagen shampoos promise to leave you with a fuller head of hair, while we're also told that washing your hair less frequently can train it to become less greasy. But how much of this viral advice is actually supported by science? Some are fact, some are fiction. Trichologist Anabel Kingsley, whose new book, Haircare: The Ultimate Guide, explores the relationship between women's health and hair, says it's important to distinguish between the trends and treatments that are actually backed by scientific evidence. So here's a breakdown of what the most popular hair hacks actually do to your scalp and hair – and whether they're worth trying. Rosemary oil has managed to enjoy great PR online, from scalp-oiling tutorials to elaborate overnight routines; it's often promoted as a natural alternative to chemical hair-loss treatments.

stories.title: COP31 must accelerate delivery on targets - climate chief
stories.summary: The United Nations climate chief has warned that global action is "nowhere near fast or fair enough", urging countries at the COP31 conference in Turkey to turn existing promises into practical measures that protect communities and cut emissions. Thousands of participants have descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish city of Antalya for the UN's annual climate talks. In his opening address to the climate summit, Simon Stiell said rising fossil fuel costs were hurting households and economies, while countries vulnerable to climate change faced immense frustration accessing promised financial support. He said previous summits had set global targets and helped change the direction of investment. But this year's conference must accelerate delivery. "So, as well as sending signals, COP31 must supercharge solutions," he said. That means breaking down global commitments and national climate plans into practical steps, including expanding renewable energy, strengthening electricity grids and reducing methane emissions.

stories.title: How often should you be working at the office?
stories.summary: Analysis: While there's no single magic number, evidence suggests two to three days days in the office – and on the same days as your colleagues Office attendance from Monday to Friday used to be a pretty standard requirement for many jobs, but plenty of employees have now developed a taste for working from home. In response, some of their employers have started to tighten the rules on hybrid work. Barclays Bank is one of latest big companies to do so, telling thousands of staff they must be in the office at least three days a week instead of two. So what is the right balance for those who split the locations of their working week? Plenty of research has now been done on that question. And while it does not give a single magic number, the evidence does suggest that the best range is two or three days in the office – on the same days as your colleagues. For example, in a study involving a large online travel agency in China, more than 1,500 engineers, marketing and finance staff were allowed to work from home on Wednesdays and Fridays, while a control group stayed in the office full time. Over the following two years of performance reviews, the performance of the hybrid workers was equal in quality to those who stayed in the office. Those who worked from home were much less likely to leave the company – especially women and the workers with long commutes. A smaller experiment at an international development organisation went a step further, by randomly varying how many days 148 staff spent in the office. Those who came in around two days a week said they had a better work-life balance, more job satisfaction and less isolation than colleagues who came in more or less often. Their performance was unaffected.

stories.title: Pride for Connolly after tumultuous year ends with cup
stories.summary: Derry City interim manager Mark Connolly was delighted to see his side finish a challenging season on a high by claiming the Club Orange Men's FAI Cup. The Candystripes were 1-0 winners over Waterford at Aviva Stadium, with Darragh Burns getting the only goal of an edgy contest. Connolly returned to the Brandywell in June as the Director of Football but found himself in the hotseat after the dismissal of Tiernan Lynch in early August. From there, Derry were able to turn things around, with their cup success securing lucrative European soccer for next summer. For Connolly, it was a satisfying conclusion to a tough few months in the job. "It's been a tough number of months for myself coming back into the club. Just trying to get stuff back in place and trying to get the good times back, get the city back on side.

stories.title: Sixth couple eliminated from Strictly Come Dancing
stories.summary: House of the Dragon actress Bethany Antonia and her professional partner Nancy Xu have become the sixth couple to be eliminated from Strictly Come Dancing following a tense dance-off. The pair lost their place in the competition after head judge Shirley Ballas cast the deciding vote during Sunday night's results show. Antonia and Xu reprised their foxtrot to Bleeding Love by Leona Lewis, which had earned them 30 points on Saturday, placing them joint fourth on the leaderboard. They faced former Love Island contestant Cach Mercer and his partner Maddie Ingoldsby, who performed their waltz to That Ain’t You by Mulaa Joans, having scored 26 points on Saturday. After both couples performed, Anton Du Beke voted to save Mercer and Ingoldsby, while Craig Revel Horwood and Motsi Mabuse chose to save Antonia and Xu. With the judges divided, Ballas had the casting vote and opted to save Mercer and Ingoldsby, ending Antonia and Xu’s time in the competition.

stories.title: Russell Brand to be sentenced for rape and assaults
stories.summary: British comedian and actor Russell Brand will be sentenced today for raping a young woman and sexually assaulting three other women. Brand, 51, was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court in London of raping a woman in 2009, as well as sexually assaulting female TV and radio workers between 2004 and 2009. Mr Justice Joel Bennathan ordered Brand to start his prison sentence immediately after being found guilty last Thursday afternoon. The judge is expected to hear impact statements from Brand's victims and legal submissions from lawyers before passing sentence. Brand's wife, Laura Gallacher, has arrived at Southwark Crown Court in a minivan ahead of her husband’s sentencing. A woman held tight to Mrs Gallacher’s shoulders as they walked briskly past the press cameras into the courthouse at about 9.20am.

stories.title: State Man to get Punchestown farewell
stories.summary: Retired superstar State Man will be paraded on William Hill Morgiana Hurdle day at Punchestown on Saturday week. The Willie Mullins-trained chestnut won 14 of his 20 career starts and was six from seven at Punchestown, a record which featured back-to-back Morgiana Hurdle wins and a hat-trick of victories in the Punchestown Champion Hurdle. Paul Townend, who steered State Man to all but one of his wins, singled out State Man's 2025 showdown with Constitution Hill at Punchestown as a particularly special occasion, reflecting on the extraordinary reception the horse received from the record-breaking crowd. He said: "The reception he got at Punchestown was incredible and it was probably because of the build-up to the showdown between ourselves and Constitution Hill when they were both coming back from Cheltenham falls to redeem themselves. People really got behind him that day and it was a huge performance." In all, State Man won 12 Grade Ones including the Champion Hurdle at the 2024 Cheltenham Festival and three editions of the Irish Champion Hurdle at Leopardstown. With his retirement recently confirmed, the nine-year-old is set to return to County Kildare for a final lap of honour on 21 November.

stories.title: Trump 'only kidding' over press role offer to UFC boss
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has said he was only joking when he offered the role of White House press secretary to Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White at the weekend. "I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea," Mr Trump told reporters on the tarmac of his namesake airport in Florida. The press secretary role - traditionally one of the administration's most visible positions - has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on 16 October after less than a week on the job. Mr White, the 57-year-old president and CEO of UFC, is a long-time friend of the president. Speaking in London late Saturday, Mr White was reticent, saying that he would "have more to talk about" after meeting with Mr Trump today. Mr White's UFC staged a bloody cage fight on the White House South Lawn on Mr Trump's 80th birthday in June, and he appeared on stage with Mr Trump during his re-election victory speech in 2024.

stories.summary: Green Bay Packers thrashed New England Patriots 45-27 as Jordan Love threw for 372 yards to strengthen his MVP odds. The quarterback threw for three touchdowns and rushed for another during Green Bay's fifth win in six games. Green Bay took an early lead at Gillette Stadium, but the Patriots fought back to reduce the deficit to 24-14 at half-time. But the Packers pulled away in the third quarter, establishing a commanding lead the Patriots were unable to close. Meanwhile, CJ Stroud threw for 384 yards and Houston Texans surged to a 44-22 win over Los Angeles Chargers. The Texans improved to a 3-5 record on the season with their third win in four games while Los Angeles slumped to 0-8 in their worst season start in franchise history.

stories.title: Tánaiste's unemployment comments a 'Tory soundbite' - SF
stories.summary: Sinn Féin's spokesperson on social protection has described the Tánaiste's comments on unemployment as "straight out of the Tory playbook". Louise O'Reilly said Tánaiste Simon Harris could have said he wanted supports in place for the unemployed or to be able to access work "but instead he delivered a cheap, pathetic Tory soundbite". At the Fine Gael ard fheis in Cork at the weekend, Tánaiste Simon Harris pledged to penalise long-term unemployed people who refuse to engage with services to get them back to work. Mr Harris said that it was not acceptable for people to be out of work at a time of full employment, adding that "the dole is a safety net, not a way of life". Mr Harris said: "At a time of full employment, it is simply not acceptable for any person to remain on the Live Register year after year after year." "We need a renewed focus on intensive engagement with the long-term unemployed - tackling barriers, creating opportunities and getting people into work.

stories.title: Brentford players need to be more streetwise - Andrews
stories.summary: Head coach Keith Andrews wants his Brentford players to become more streetwise in the face of perceived provocation following Sunday's frustrating 2-0 Premier League defeat at Brighton. The Bees faced an uphill battle at the Amex Stadium when striker Igor Thiago was sent off in the 23rd minute after raising an arm towards the face of Albion midfielder Chema Andres during an altercation. Brentford trailed to Diego Gomez’s stunning strike at that stage and were left with little way back after Pascal Gross converted a penalty following Keane Lewis-Potter’s shirt tug on Luka Vuskovic. The Bees’ only other top-flight defeat this term was last month’s 2-1 home loss to Liverpool, in which Yehor Yarmoliuk was dismissed for headbutting Jeremy Jacquet as the pair grappled at a corner. "We need to grow as a group, react in better ways," Andrews told Brentford’s website. "We obviously gave them a leg-up with the sending-off and the penalty. It then becomes very difficult.

stories.summary: Nvidia has said its board was probing whether CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, after a media report alleged he had a close relationship with a ⁠Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. Mr Huang said in a message to employees that he had been "unfaithful" to his wife and took "full responsibility" for his actions, while Nvidia said the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company without interruption. The developments are likely to pressure the chipmaker's stock, which has already fallen sharply amid worries about the AI boom's sustainability, and may also raise questions about his future at the helm of the company he co-founded, analysts said. The New York Times reported last month that Mr Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. Mr Huang admitted to having been unfaithful to his wife, saying, "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I ⁠did. I am deeply sorry." Addressing his colleagues, board, partners and shareholders, he said: "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn ⁠back your confidence."

stories.title: Krakow shooting suspect dies in hospital, say police
stories.summary: The alleged perpetrator of a deadly weekend shooting spree in Krakow has died, Polish police said, two days after he was critically wounded in a shootout with officers. "We inform you that the perpetrator of the tragic events died this morning in the hospital," regional police said in a post on X of the 24-year-old Polish man who allegedly opened fire on Saturday in central Krakow, killing six people. Authorities said the man had been "fascinated by far-right ideologies" and Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the shooting - the deadliest in the country since the end of communism in 1989 - an act of "terrorism". Six people, including two foreigners, were killed in the shooting spree, and about 15 others were wounded, according to authorities. The gunman is suspected to have killed nine people in total after the bodies of three people - his parents and sister - were found at their home two hours' drive from Krakow. Meanwhile, Poland is facing a week of political tensions after the shooting shattered residents' sense of security in the deeply divided nation.

stories.title: Top-10 finish for Power in Mexico as Brown wins play-off
stories.summary: Séamus Power enjoyed a strong finish to the World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico to finish tied for eighth, five shots behind tournament winner Blades Brown. At 19 years, five months and 18 days old, Brown is nearly six months younger than Jordan Spieth was when the three-time major champion claimed his first win at the 2013 John Deere Classic, the last time the tour had a teenage winner. Power, who had excelled in Saturday's third round with a 65, almost matched that in Sunday's closing round. The Waterford man carded a six-under 66 to finish the tournament on 18 under. Power got off on the wrong foot with a bogey on the first. But things would only get better from there on the El Cardonal at Diamante course at Cabo San Lucas. A birdie on the third had him pointing in the right direction and three holes later, an eagle on the par-5 sixth had him two under for the day.

stories.title: State thalidomide apology long overdue, says campaigner
stories.summary: A State apology for people affected by the drug, thalidomide, is long overdue and costs nothing, a spokesperson for the Irish Thalidomide Association has said. Finola Cassidy was responding to comments by Tánaiste Simon Harris, who said yesterday that he would like a State apology to be delivered this year. Thalidomide was prescribed to pregnant women in the 1950s and 1960s as a treatment for morning sickness, but was later withdrawn because of its links to birth defects and lifelong disabilities. The German manufacturer apologised in 2012 to those born without limbs as a result of its use. "An apology costs nothing, you know, and maybe we don't need another Christmas to pass without receiving it. "I feel very strongly that it's long overdue and, you know, an apology in itself will have to be meaningful."

stories.title: Commission seeks information on sexual abuse in schools
stories.summary: The Commission of Investigation examining the handling of historical child sexual abuse in schools has called on members of the public here and abroad to come forward with any information that could help its work. A survey launched by the commission last month has received hundreds of responses, but the team is keen to hear from others before it closes on 7 December. New information has emerged in relation to schools that were not previously examined, which is why the commission is appealing for more people to take the survey. The Commission of Investigation's remit relates to the handling of concerns relating to child sexual abuse in all schools between 1927 and 2013. It was established after a Scoping Inquiry into day and boarding schools run by religious orders revealed widespread historical abuse. The commission's work is much wider than the Scoping Inquiry. As a statutory body, it holds far more power, enabling it, for example, to compel witnesses and documentation.

stories.title: Call for roll-out of lung cancer screening programme
stories.summary: The Irish Cancer Society has called for a national lung cancer screening programme to be rolled out. Chief Executive Nikki Gallagher said a successful pilot programme to identify early-stage lung cancer has already demonstrated proof of concept, and should be prioritised. The participants were ex-smokers who were aged between 55 and 74. Of those 10,000, around 2,500 were invited to take part in a scan, and 40 asymptomatic people were identified with early-stage lung cancer. "It is really unheard of to identify lung cancer at such an early stage," she said, adding many of these people have already been treated successfully. "Lung cancer takes more Irish lives than any other cancer. So the idea that this lung cancer pilot can give hope to anybody else involved in the project is wonderful.

stories.title: Magnificent seven for Derry as Burns sinks Waterford
stories.summary: Derry City further enhanced their reputation as cup specialists with a 1-0 victory over Waterford in the Club Orange Men's FAI Cup final this afternoon at Aviva Stadium. Darragh Burns got the only goal of the game with a fine strike from the edge of the box midway through the second half to secure a seventh cup triumph for the Candystripes since joining the League of Ireland in 1985. For the Blues, it's another defeat in the decider, 22 years after their last one, with their 46-year wait for a victory set to go on for another season, at least. A crowd of 36,093 paid in to watch a stop-start decider, which the Blues shaded for a good chunk of the middle of the game, but Derry showed that little bit of ruthlessness to get over the line. While the Ulstermen had finished two places higher in the League of Ireland, Waterford had been in better form coming into the game, having also recorded a more recent victory in clashes between the sides. But it's Derry who will be heading for Europe next summer, not before the celebrations kick into gear this evening; their league disappointment and the James McClean saga now long behind them.

"We see this again, punching down at people instead of punching up where the real issues are," he said.
